analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/...). They add no production code, endpoints, key handling, attestation paths or cache storage changes, so none of the TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-011 controls or the T-041 prefix-cache posture are altered.

GLM5NextPromptPolicyTests.swift (head 509-908): tests cover reasoning/thinking/clear_thinking control precedence. The tests assert that forged internal marker 'x-darkbloom-original-boolean-schema' is rejected only when actual model_type is glm5_next (lines 603-619); the llama path intentionally keeps the old treatment of coordinator-owned markers. That asserts existing behavior and is not a new regression. Other tests cover tool-call history correlation, argument validation, exact large integers and rejection of inexact ones (898-907), and OpenRouter request shapes being served.

GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift: adds a CryptoKit import, a GLMMediaMarkerTokenizer stub, and an openRouterVideo helper that reads fixture clips from a repo-relative path (via #filePath, 6 parents up) and verifies SHA-256, so fixtures are integrity-pinned. It also adds a test that sends video data URIs through the scheduler with real GLM5NextProcessor ingest. Sanitized failure codes are checked via ProviderLoop.sanitizedInferenceFailure. There is no secret material in the fixtures and no network access.

I saw no weakened assertions that would hide a security regression. The visible head text is partial for the media test file (only the patch is available), so I did not evaluate the production changes that those tests imply (variable-frame-rate QuickTime ingest, thinking-object parsing, strict-tool handling). Those production changes are outside this batch and should be reviewed where they land. Particular points: media decode bounds and budget reservation for newly accepted video types, and the tolerant parsing of previously rejected 'thinking'/'reasoning' shapes.
